chunks: Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Amr ibn Abī al-Miqdām, from his father, who said:

I passed by al-Baqī‘ with Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him), and we walked by the grave of a man from among the Shia of Kūfah. I said to Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is the grave of one of the Shia.'

He stopped by it and said: 'O Allāh! Have mercy on his isolation; connect with him in his loneliness; keep him company in his desolation; make him feel safe in his fear; descend Your Mercy on him in a way that he will not need the mercy of others; and join him with those whom he loved.'

key_terms.الْبَقِيعِ: Al-Baqi', a famous cemetery in Medina
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّاهُ: Those who loved or had guardianship over him

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for the deceased Shia in al-Baqi?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarah* highlights the Imam’s personal engagement with the spiritual state of the common believer, specifically addressing the concept of 'ghurbah' (spiritual or physical alienation) prevalent in Shia tradition. The supplication emphasizes divine self-sufficiency ('istighna') over intercession by others, reflecting a nuanced theological stance on direct reliance on God. It serves as a model for ziyarah that combines emotional comfort with doctrinal clarity regarding the afterlife.
